system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

    SMB aggressive discounting: +31% signups, -12% retention. Low-LTV trap. Retire unless fit improves.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and two independent inherited records (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on cutting required signup fields) say improvements there produced durable lift in completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation. That makes simplify_onboarding the direction with the best claim on sustainable qualified revenue, so I spend both verification pulls on exactly the two memories the decision rests on rather than on memories I am not acting on. I explicitly decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records +31% signups against -12% retention and labels it a low-LTV trap, which is directly contrary to the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; matching a competitor's discount would buy the wrong accounts. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the credible runner-up and is what I would move to if verification shows memory_86's lift was small, confounded, or measured on a cohort unlike today's. Key downstream risk I want on the record: 'simplification' by cutting required signup fields reduces the firmographic data captured at intake, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert through sales-assisted demo-request flows that depend on that data for routing and qualification. So an intervention that lifts raw activation can quietly degrade pipeline quality — the exact metric the objective cares about. Hence a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: hold enterprise/demo-request paths out of the change, keep any dropped fields to non-qualifying ones, and instrument qualified-pipeline and lead-routing quality alongside completion and activation, with a stop rule if qualification degrades. Remaining uncertainty I am not resolving this week: I do not know that onboarding friction caused the QoQ declines rather than competitor-driven mix shift toward less-committed price-sensitive traffic, in which case a funnel fix would be treating a symptom of an acquisition-mix problem. The verification pulls are aimed partly at whether the archived lifts were durable and measured on comparable cohorts, which is what would distinguish these.
